review.headline: A slow Giuoco Pianissimo where you converted a queenside attack and won on time

sections.text: You played a classical Italian with 4.d3, 5.Be3 and 6.Nbd2. After 7.h3 Bxf3 8.Qxf3 you had the bishop pair, a good start, and you pressed on with 9.Bg5 and 11.Bh4.
15.Nf3?! was a small slip, and 15...O-O-O? from Black missed 15...Qg7. Then 16.Bd5?? gave back the edge, since 16.Qxf7 was stronger. Black replied 16...Na5??, which was another error.
You rebuilt with 17.b4 and 18.Bxc6?!, then played the pawn break 20.a4 and the strong 22.a5!. Black's king on the c8 square had no good cover.
24.Rfb1? was a small mistake, where 24.Nd2 was better, but Black replied 24...Ka8??. You found 25.b6! and 27.Ra7+, and won on time with a strong position.

review.turning_point: 22.a5! and 25.b6! broke open the king's position on the queenside.
review.focus: At move 16, 16.Bd5 threw away a clear chance. 16.Qxf7 took a pawn with the queen already on h5. Check every capture before choosing a quieter move.
